cells.tense: The pen is in your hand right now, and you are seeing clearly.
cells.act: return to the work daily until it is profound
cells.ask: Settle on a practice that takes a real hour. Do it today and again tomorrow, the same way. Keep the method you started with until it has had time. Ask only how far you got.
cells.core:
You can tell what matters from what doesn't, and you do it by hand, alone, without announcing anything. Out at the edge of what you know, that attention holds. You come back to the same problem day after day and it gets sharper under your fingers, and you are not doing this at anyone. But you can feel what the person across from you is carrying as plainly as your own heartbeat, and you haven't said so.

The careful work and the company you keep run on separate tracks. Choose how you'll practice and hold to it — same hour, same problem, same method for a good stretch. Then let the practice run where somebody can see it, once. They don't have to comment. What gets built when it's seen continues differently than what gets built alone.
cells.sheetLine: Come back to the same problem daily and watch it sharpen.
cells.verb: refining, through close attention, what is worth keeping and what is not
cells.place: a room where someone else's state is felt as clearly as your own, and you would rather not say so out loud

cells.tense: The reckoning is being done in advance for something that hasn't happened yet.
cells.act: make the sacrifice visible without explaining it
cells.ask: Say to the person it was for one sentence about what you did and got no word about. No story, no explanation, then stop talking.
cells.core:
You are already working out what people will need before they need it, and none of it has happened. The refining has turned into forecasting — what will go wrong, who will need what, which effort of yours will go unseen. Your care for people, which is real, is being spent ahead of time, in your own head, and the hours it takes sit in there with it. What you give keeps being given quietly, and quiet is starting to feel like the price.

The work itself is not the problem. The hiddenness is. Choose a person and say the plain sentence about what you have been carrying for them — in the open, no explanation attached. You will find out whether they know. That answer is worth more than the forecast. Then keep the same care, out loud, now and then.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying for people what they haven't seen you carry.
cells.verb: refining, through close attention, what is worth keeping and what is not

cells.tense: The door closed behind you and you're still standing there anyway.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Remember someone you gave to lately. When they offer you something small — a ride, a coffee, a hand with one job — say yes, and then stop steering.
cells.core:
You are still working out what people needed from what the moment called for, and you have kept at it since. Out here, where another person's state and yours meet, you've gone quiet. You would say you are being considerate, and you probably are. Reaching back out has stopped being something you do, and the room you are in has gotten smaller than you noticed.

The way through is not more effort from you. It moves the other direction. Take something small from someone this week — a lift, a coffee, a hand with one job — and receive it plainly. What you give can then be given again instead of counted. One exchange does work that a hundred anticipations cannot.

cells.tense: The pen has already been at this page, and it wasn't reported as yours.
cells.act: savour the realised thing without reaching past it
cells.ask: Take something you already have that works — the pot you like, a tool, a finished piece. Use it as it is, without improving it while you use it. Stop there.
cells.core:
You have been making distinctions for people for a long stretch, and both accounts say the same thing: that's just how you are. What got built was built by your eye — what was worth saying and what got dropped, what was worth keeping and what got let go. That you did it is folded into the record as terrain, not as work. Nobody has a reason to correct you, and you don't either.

What comes before all the refining is liking things. There's a version of you that simply enjoyed what was there. Take something you already have that works and use it as it is this week, without quietly improving it while you use it. Enjoy it and stop there. What you made is already finished, and saying so is enough.
